text:
maya: Heads-up — infra CI is failing on the gpu infra repo. terraform-apply starts, GH runner preempts a GPU node mid-release, helm install times out and rolls back. Seen across 2 runs in the last hour.
sam: Can you paste the failing logs? which job exactly?
maya: job is .github/workflows/infra.yml -> terraform-apply -> deploy-helm. Logs show timeout during Helm pre-install hook then node eviction. Also saw cache-restore retry earlier.
ci-bot: [deploy] terraform apply: acquiring lock... error: apply timed out; subsequent helm release failed.
arjun: This looks like a node-drain race: autoscaler/spot preemption removes node while helm hook pods are still running. Helm's --wait then times out and triggers rollback.
lina: We also had a 403 on cache restore earlier which increased job runtime, making the window for preemption more likely. Noticed GKE spot termination events around the same timestamps.
maya: snippet from helm logs: ```
Error: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists. Unable to continue with install: hook pre-install failed: pod "gpu-init-abc123" evicted
helm performed rollback for release "gpu-canary"
```
sam: Oof. Two pieces to address: (1) reduce chance of eviction while a deploy is in-flight, (2) make deploys resilient to in-flight node drains.
arjun: For (1) we can temporarily tag GH Actions runners with node-pool that is non-preemptible for terraform/helm jobs, or add a short runner affinity to avoid spot nodes during critical steps. For (2) change helm hooks to tolerate eviction and extend timeouts.
lina: Another quick mitigation is introducing a pre-deploy step that drains targeted nodes from receiving new pods while we roll, using cordon+drain with grace. But careful: draining the wrong node can spike pending pods.
maya: Example quick-change I tested locally: add a small hook step before helm install: ```bash
NODE=$(kubectl get pods -l app=gpu-init -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.nodeName}')
kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 &
``` worked to prevent the eviction mid-hook in my dry run. Not ideal for prod though.
sam: We should not rely on ad-hoc cordon in CI. Better: in GH Actions use concurrency and an explicit lock to serialize terraform/helm apply across runners so two parallel jobs don't collide with autoscaler flapping. Example concurrency block: ```yaml
concurrency:
  group: infra-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
Plus add a step that bumps a repo-scoped lock file (or use a tiny DynamoDB/Consul lock) to ensure only one infra apply at a time.
arjun: Also propose enabling graceful termination handling in our init containers: intercept SIGTERM and wait for kubelet eviction grace period to finish for critical hook actions. That reduces failure rate when preemptions happen.
maya: Could also increase helm timeout per release: `helm upgrade --install --wait --timeout 10m` for releases that run expensive init hooks.
lina: On the cache side, we should harden restore step backoff and avoid extended stalls. The 403 came from the artifact proxy returning a transient 403 during credential refresh; add retry logic with jitter. That reduces chance of long jobs running during preemption windows.
sam: Action items I can take: (A) add concurrency to infra workflows and a repo-level lock step, (B) bump helm timeout for gpu-pool releases to 10m in canary only, (C) add a small change to runners: prefer non-preemptible pool for terraform/helm jobs.
maya: I'll open a PR for the helm timeout + hook resilience changes (small change to hook pod's preStop to sleep 30s).
arjun: I'll draft a small init-container patch to catch SIGTERM and wait on a net-check before failing (will put as opt-in env var).
ci-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3242 to track: "GH Actions infra apply failures — node drain / helm rollback race".
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused automatically until infra PR merges.
maya: Plan to run a canary after the concurrency + helm timeout changes. If that looks good we'll roll to staging and then prod next week. :thumbsup:
sam: Sounds good. For the repo lock we can use a tiny `state-lock` action that creates/releases a GCS object with `generation` semantics to avoid extra infra. I'll prototype today.
lina: I'll also add a retry wrapper for cache restore to avoid 403 spikes lengthening runs.
maya: thanks, will report back with canary results here.
